page_title: Tokenized Money Market Funds — Digital Assets Dashboard
page_subtitle_html: Tokenized money market fund (MMF) exposure aggregated from RWA.xyz US Treasuries and Non-U.S. Government Debt. Networks and platforms are built from each fund's on-chain token deployments; Distributed Value columns are current levels.
kpi_window_note: Distributed value uses a 30-day (30D) % change vs summed token values 30 days ago. Top network share is the largest network by distributed value; the 30D figure is the change in market-share percentage points (pp), not a percent of total. Fund universe: fixed curated TMMF population on RWA.xyz US Treasuries and Non-U.S. Government Debt; KPIs, charts, and league tables use the same fund set.
key_observations_html:
Key observations

  • TMMF distributed value fell 10.0% over 30D: With distributed value at $13.47B (10.0% lower over 30D), tokenized-cash balances look lighter—suggesting some institutions pulled liquidity or rotated away from TMMF wrappers even if headline product news stayed busy. Related: Franklin Templeton Fund Shares Become Bybit Trading Collateral (The Defiant).
  • Early "flight to efficiency" shows up in TMMF 30D network share: Among tokenized money market funds, gainers include BNB Chain (+1.70% 30D TMMF network share), Solana (+1.51% 30D TMMF network share); losers include Ethereum (-4.12% 30D TMMF network share), Mantle (-0.19% 30D TMMF network share). That pattern is consistent with TMMF issuers routing more distributed value toward higher-throughput, lower-fee chains—though Ethereum still dominates TMMF share levels in most snapshots.
  • Regulatory framing still decides product access: Similar funds can sit under different investor-eligibility and jurisdiction labels, so compliance framing still decides who can hold and distribute them. Related: Clarity Act’s failure gave crypto ‘faster’ regulatory wins, Bitwise CIO says (The Block).
  • Rates still matter as much as product and chain choice: Rate and money-market moves can reshape fund-level inflows as quickly as any chain or product launch story. Related: Live updates: Bitcoin posts tentative gains as rates drop ahead of Friday's jobs report (CoinDesk).
  • Issuer strategies are splitting into two models: Institutional cash rail programs (low holder counts, large AUM per holder—e.g. USYC, BUIDL, iBENJI, JLTXX) vs global yield / distribution products (broader holder bases, retail- or UCITS-friendly framing—e.g. USDY, WTGXX, BENJI, USTBL). These behave like different businesses under the same "tokenized MMF" label. Related: U.S. SEC maps out crypto custody in new proposal that furthers its digital assets agenda (CoinDesk).

Context only—not investment advice. Observations rank fund-level and network aggregates on this page against recent tokenization and money-market headlines. Bullets combine on-page data with recent industry headlines.

Key observations are AI generated and should be reviewed for accuracy.
